assumptions.summary: Assumes global warming does not noticeably improve during the next 50 years.

models.summary: encoded SST scaling, sentinel handling, and Scotland-domain crop: Convert the Hadley SST archive to Celsius and retain the 57-65 N, 20 W-4 E grid used by all later forecasts. It hands off T, Omega, M.
grey relational analysis of SST change and global drivers: Rank greenhouse emissions, forest area, and population by average grey relational grade against SST change. It hands off r_i.
first-order accumulated grey differential equation: Smooth an SST sequence by accumulated generation and represent its evolution with a two-parameter GM(1,1) equation. It hands off X1.

least-squares estimation with adjacent-mean background values: Estimate the GM development and input coefficients from accumulated background values and original observations. It hands off theta, z_k.
closed-form grey response and inverse accumulated generation: Generate future accumulated SST values and restore them to the original sequence scale. It hands off X1_hat, X0_hat.
residual variance ratio for grey forecast acceptance: Compare residual variance with original SST variance and summarize the selected validation example by C=S2/S1. It hands off e_k, S1, S2, C.
three-path SST scenario envelope: Convert a central SST path and unspecified annual bounds into best, most-likely, and worst migration scenarios. It hands off T_low, T_mid, T_high.
species-weighted SST-salinity-bathymetry suitability score: Combine three environmental layers with separate herring and mackerel weights to create a habitat index. It hands off E.

species score interval and local stasis tolerance: Represent preferred environmental-index ranges and suppress movement when the current score is sufficiently near a species optimum. It hands off I_stay.
annual local-neighborhood habitat selection: Move each species center to the most suitable cell in a self-centered 3x3 neighborhood unless the comfort rule keeps it stationary. It hands off r_next.

circular Gaussian catch field with a 120-km coastal mask: Spread catch around a moving species center and sum the portion overlapping the assumed accessible Scottish fishing area. It hands off q, Q_access.
first-zero accessible-catch event: Record the first forecast year when the modeled shoal no longer overlaps the accessible Scottish fishing area. It hands off tau.

models.section: 6.1 fleet cost, income, and net profit
models.summary: fleet-level fixed-cost and species catch-price profit: Combine a 2.5-percent share of EU vessel count, average boat cost, accessible species catch, and price into annual net profit curves. It hands off TFC, TFP, NP.
undisclosed long-horizon EU fleet-count forecast: Supply CFR values from 2020 through 2069 to the fleet-cost term in the profit model. It hands off CFR_fore.

models.section: 6.2 two-step domestic and overseas asset strategy
models.summary: rule-based phased relocation and mixed-fleet strategy: Encode the prose recommendation to relocate west-coast assets immediately, move north-coast assets in 20-percent five-year stages, and use a 50-percent long-endurance fleet before the overseas decision. It hands off A_move, L_share, D.

country resistance multiplier on fishing cost: Compare domestic Shetland profit with Iceland or Norway by multiplying fishing cost by designated country resistance coefficients. It hands off TFC_foreign, NP_foreign.
one-at-a-time relative perturbation diagnostics: Measure endpoint location, average catch, and average profit responses to plus or minus 0.1-percent parameter changes. It hands off Delta_pos, R_Y.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge can recover the forecast-to-strategy chain from eight compact paragraphs, but the confidence language must remain bounded.
Five explicit work bullets make the promised modules easy to trace into the body.
Separate herring and mackerel paths answer the two-species requirement more clearly than a combined endpoint.
The 2020-2040 and 2040-2070 phases produce a memorable decision narrative, subject to missing cost optimization.
The article is vivid and audience-aware but exceeds the official one-page limit and overstates several modeled claims.

weaknesses.summary: The exact Hadley dataset/version, download date, and code used to scale or mask the archive are not reported.
The appendix shows scaled values such as -10 and -1.8 but does not distinguish sea-ice sentinels from legitimate cold water after division by 100.
The phrase 150*9*25 'in years' ambiguously mixes time count and spatial dimensions, and no month-to-year aggregation is defined.
Integer latitude-longitude cells vary in physical width and receive no projection or area correction.
The local crop is 57-65 N and 20 W-4 E, but later distance, circle, and territorial statements treat degree cells as uniform physical space.
The report alternates between 1980-2019 and an original sequence from 1980 to 2020, changing the fitted sample size.
A claimed 1970 cold wave is used to discard earlier data without citation, changepoint test, or sensitivity to the chosen 1980 window.
Forty years of local data are described as insufficient for a 50-year forecast, but the grey model does not create new information that resolves that horizon mismatch.
The report does not publish the exact 20 years, units, normalization, or alignment of SST, emissions, forest, and population sequences.
The distinguishing coefficient rho is not assigned a value and collides with the notation-table description of rho as an impact ratio.
The printed grey relational coefficient has ambiguous min/max indices and does not explicitly define the absolute deviation term.
Grey relational grade measures shape proximity after preprocessing; it does not establish causal impact on SST.
Table 2 labels greenhouse emissions and forest area under Human Factors and population under Environmental Factor, reversing the stated conceptual grouping.
The two group grades 0.9988 and 0.6423 are not derived from the three listed subfactor grades by any disclosed aggregation.
No uncertainty, null comparison, lag analysis, multicollinearity check, or out-of-sample relevance accompanies the near-one relation grades.
The correlation analysis is rhetorically used to promise an enhanced forecast, but its grades never enter a displayed forecasting equation.
The report calls the model enhanced with greenhouse, forest, and population factors, but the displayed GM(1,1) state has only a constant b.
Independent GM(1,1) fits at 225 cells omit spatial dependence and shared ocean dynamics.
One exponential law is extrapolated 50 years without coefficient stability, nonexplosion, or physical temperature bounds.
Directly inverting B^T B receives no rank, conditioning, numerical-stability, or parameter-uncertainty check.
The background-value formula is typographically ambiguous in the rendered source and no numerical example resolves its indices.
No fitted a or b value is reported for even the Table 3 example, so the displayed forecast cannot be reproduced.
The response equation receives no special treatment for a near zero, where b/a is unstable.
The printed response indices and prose alternate x-hat superscripts/subscripts without a consistent one-step horizon convention.
The report does not show how monthly archive values become the annual X0 sequence used in inverse accumulation.
The appendix publishes SST forecasts only through 2048 for a few columns, not the complete 225-cell path through 2070.
No prediction interval, parameter uncertainty, residual model, or spatial covariance accompanies the 2045 and 2070 surfaces.
The paper says 20 locations are used as validation but does not identify them or explain whether validation is spatial, temporal, or both.
Table 3 contains 15 years from 2005 through 2019, not a transparent 20-location acceptance calculation.
Only one cell's residual series is shown, so C=0.55 cannot validate all 225 locations.
The paper gives no acceptance threshold or grey accuracy grade, so C=0.55 is not self-evidently a 'small level'.
The 2019 prediction 7.727 C differs from the actual 3.8316 C by 3.8954 C, larger than the actual value itself.
Residuals become persistently negative and grow after 2010, indicating systematic upward forecast bias rather than random error.
The strength claim of higher accuracy contradicts the acknowledged large final-year deviation and lacks a baseline forecast.
The posterior ratio does not test the decision-relevant 2020-2070 extrapolation horizon.
SST, salinity, and bathymetry have different units and are added without normalization, so E has no coherent physical scale.
The equation uses BM while the notation and prose use SD or bathymetry; BM is never defined.
Expert weights are reported without experts, elicitation method, data fit, uncertainty, or external habitat validation.
Although each weight row sums to one, this does not make unscaled inputs comparable.
The 1980-2018 mean salinity and depth fields are frozen for 50 years while only SST changes, making temperature dominate future score changes by construction.
The SST source is described here as ICES data despite the earlier Hadley archive statement, and the interface between sources is not explained.
Five-year catch maps are treated as habitat observations without correcting for fishing effort, fleet access, quota, or market targeting.
Table 5 comfort intervals are said to come from the longest living environment and previous studies, but no derivation or species data are shown.
The prose says the example fish prefers index 6.75, the Figure 4 center is 6.2, and both exceed or conflict with the displayed species comfort limits.
The broad Table 5 interval and separate absolute tolerance 0.1 define two incompatible stay rules without precedence.
The single optimum E_opt required by the 0.1 rule is never reported for either species.
The assumptions allow movement within two grids per year, but the described 3x3 neighborhood permits only one cell from the center.
No rule handles ties, coast/land candidates, domain edges, diagonals, or a local optimum that traps the greedy path.
A one-cell move has different kilometers in latitude, longitude, and diagonal directions, but all choices are treated equally.
The model moves only one center per species and has no population mass, spread dynamics, births, deaths, or multiple subpopulations.
Initializing at the most-fished cell confounds biological abundance with historical effort and ignores uncertainty in the five-year map.
The claimed onset around 2040 is read from the generated path but receives no threshold, changepoint calculation, or observed migration validation.
Mackerel is variously described as moving toward Canada, Iceland, and through the Faroe Islands without one coordinate endpoint ledger.
Herring is routed toward Norway/Arctic waters but later repeatedly placed at 'South Shetland Islands,' a different hemisphere.
Migration omits currents, prey, spawning, fishing mortality, salinity change, depth accessibility, density feedback, and species interaction.
The upper and lower SST paths used as best and worst cases have no confidence level, residual construction, or probability.
Calling the central path 'most likely' is unsupported because the grey model supplies no forecast distribution.
A circular Gaussian in latitude-longitude degrees is not a physical circle because degree width varies with latitude.
The three-grid radius is uncalibrated and corresponds to hundreds of kilometers, materially controlling catch persistence.
The text alternates between the center as maximum catch and total fish as the Gaussian scale, so density normalization is ambiguous.
No standard deviation, truncation normalization, population conservation, growth, fishing depletion, or catchability is defined.
The cited 90/120-km fishing observation is converted into a hard universal technical limit without vessel, port, route, or preservation heterogeneity.
Distance is measured from the mainland rather than actual ports and navigable sea routes.
The statement that any shoal overlap makes the total fish catchable ignores partial overlap, effort, capacity, and travel cost.
First exact zero catch is an unstable threshold and is not the official economic-impracticality criterion.
Question marks in Table 7 are right-censored beyond 2070 but receive no survival-analysis or uncertainty treatment.
The 2044, 2063, and 2068 dates inherit undocumented SST bounds, score weights, local path ties, shoal radius, and fishing-mask assumptions.
The public article repeatedly calls loss from the modeled Scottish fishing area 'extinction,' a much stronger biological claim.
TFC is a fleet-level cost based on 2.5 percent of all EU vessels, not a small-company cost.
The 2.5-percent Scottish share is held fixed while the appendix forecasts a large decline in EU vessel count through 2069.
TFP is defined in the notation as average income per boat but Q_i P_i appears to use total accessible species catch.
Prices are written as GBP 1,070 and GBP 337 per thousand tons, an implausible and ambiguous unit not reconciled to Q_i.
Costs are in euros and revenue in pounds, but no exchange rate or common currency is applied before subtraction.
The species-specific equation subtracts the full fleet cost from each species separately and does not define combined company profit.
The prose says fleet cost is weighted by species value but publishes no weighting equation or values.
CoS is frozen at the 2010-2015 average through 2070 with no inflation, fuel price, wage, maintenance, or technology path.
No trip count, effort, quota, capacity, spoilage, demand, tax, debt, asset, cash, or company heterogeneity enters net profit.
The CFR forecast from 2020 to 2069 has no disclosed method, fit, equation, validation, or uncertainty.
A declining CFR mechanically lowers total modeled cost and can create the pre-2040 profit increase without any technology mechanism.
The conclusion attributes early profit growth to technology development, but technology is absent from all profit equations.
The report says costs remain stable while simultaneously recommending higher-cost long-endurance technology, without a scenario cost update.
The claimed worst zero-profit year around 2054 is not reconciled with the species-specific 2044 and 2068 zero-catch dates.
The mackerel domestic plot starts near 0.8 billion GBP while the prose calls it about 80 million, a roughly tenfold mismatch.
Market saturation and competition are invoked to explain a domestic decline but neither mechanism appears in the profit equation.
Immediate relocation of all west-coast assets has no port, property, permit, labor, financing, downtime, or market-delivery cost.
The 20-percent-every-five-years schedule is asserted without optimization, cash-flow simulation, or asset inventory.
The 50-percent long-endurance fleet share is asserted without capacity, purchase price, operating cost, or alternative-share comparison.
The paired catch-and-refrigeration vessel logistics omit rendezvous, transfer capacity, fuel, crew, safety, weather, and spoilage constraints.
The claim that doubling preservation time doubles range and increases catch exponentially has no equation, data, or capacity boundary.
The balance-sheet policy has no balance-sheet variables, solvency threshold, capital budget, or decision rule.
The recommended countries depend on species routes but legal access and the requested fishery proportion are not modeled.
The text alternates between Shetland Islands near Scotland and South Shetland Islands near Antarctica, making the domestic destination geographically incoherent.
The public article repeats South Shetland as a domestic Scottish destination, confirming the geographic error rather than a single typo.
One coefficient multiplies cost to represent tariffs, bilateral rules, currents, winds, navigation risk, and unexpected losses with incompatible units and mechanisms.
Norway 1.2 and Iceland 1.5 are designated without source rows, estimation, currency basis, uncertainty, or time dependence.
The existence or absence of Scottish fishing cooperation is asserted without treaty, quota, or licensing evidence.
The official requirement varies the proportion of fishery entering foreign territorial water; the model instead selects whole country destinations and has no proportion variable.
Foreign catch fields near Norway, Iceland, or the claimed South Shetland location are not published or derived from a territorial mask.
Only cost is multiplied; quotas, access limits, tariffs on revenue, port distance, foreign landing price, and legal exclusion do not change.
Figures 9 and 10 cannot be reproduced from the disclosed equations, partial appendix tables, or any code.
The prose says foreign mackerel profit begins lower at 0.5 billion than domestic profit stated as 80 million, which is arithmetically false unless the domestic text is wrong.
The foreign profit slope is described as a consequence of resistance, but a constant cost multiplier alone does not establish the claimed dynamic slope mechanism.
The conclusion that only going abroad is inevitable omits domestic technology costs, switching costs, policy uncertainty, quotas, and alternative fisheries.
Perturbing expert weights independently by 0.1 percent does not state whether the rows are renormalized to sum to one.
Endpoint displacement is measured in Euclidean degrees rather than kilometers and ignores longitude convergence.
A plus or minus 0.1-percent local perturbation is too narrow to represent uncertainty in expert weights or comfort bounds.
A 0.1-percent fishing-radius change is only 0.12 km, so the reported small catch response is not a demanding robustness test.
Country resistance coefficients are likewise moved only 0.1 percent despite being arbitrary scenario assumptions.
Average annual profit response can hide a change in crossover year or strategy ranking.
No joint parameter uncertainty, structural alternative, stochastic replication, or decision-reversal frequency is tested.
The resistance sensitivity table duplicates the Table 9 number already used for coefficient values.
The Hook Line and Sinker article spans roughly two and a half physical pages, exceeding the official one-page requirement.
The article says countless currents, winds, predators, and prey were comprehensively considered, although the migration update changes only SST.
The article claims at least a 2 C rise by 2050 even in the best case without a displayed location, aggregation, or uncertainty calculation supporting that number.
The article gives a 2056 fail-to-make-ends-meet date that is not explicitly derived or tabulated in the body.
The article presents uncosted asset percentages and vessel collaboration as a recipe for earnings rather than as unvalidated proposals.
Appendix maps and the foreign-landings graphic have no adjacent source attribution or license statement.
The appendix provides no executable code for SST forecasting, migration, catch, profit, assets, resistance, or sensitivity.
The partial CFR table stops at 2069 while the modeled horizon and conclusions extend through 2070.
The partial SST forecast table stops at 2048 and cannot support independent reconstruction of the 2070 routes.
A third-party MATHmodels Chinese QR/footer watermark appears throughout the paper and is not part of the team submission.

independent_extensions.summary: Publish exact SST, salinity, bathymetry, catch, fleet, price, and covariate datasets with a unit and transformation ledger.
Use a multivariate spatial-temporal forecast whose external drivers enter the equation, with forward holdouts and calibrated intervals.
Normalize habitat layers and fit species-specific suitability to independent herring and mackerel observations.

unresolved_questions: The exact Hadley dataset/version, download date, and code used to scale or mask the archive are not reported.
The appendix shows scaled values such as -10 and -1.8 but does not distinguish sea-ice sentinels from legitimate cold water after division by 100.
The phrase 150*9*25 'in years' ambiguously mixes time count and spatial dimensions, and no month-to-year aggregation is defined.
Integer latitude-longitude cells vary in physical width and receive no projection or area correction.
The local crop is 57-65 N and 20 W-4 E, but later distance, circle, and territorial statements treat degree cells as uniform physical space.
The report alternates between 1980-2019 and an original sequence from 1980 to 2020, changing the fitted sample size.
A claimed 1970 cold wave is used to discard earlier data without citation, changepoint test, or sensitivity to the chosen 1980 window.
Forty years of local data are described as insufficient for a 50-year forecast, but the grey model does not create new information that resolves that horizon mismatch.
The report does not publish the exact 20 years, units, normalization, or alignment of SST, emissions, forest, and population sequences.
The distinguishing coefficient rho is not assigned a value and collides with the notation-table description of rho as an impact ratio.
The printed grey relational coefficient has ambiguous min/max indices and does not explicitly define the absolute deviation term.
Grey relational grade measures shape proximity after preprocessing; it does not establish causal impact on SST.
Table 2 labels greenhouse emissions and forest area under Human Factors and population under Environmental Factor, reversing the stated conceptual grouping.
The two group grades 0.9988 and 0.6423 are not derived from the three listed subfactor grades by any disclosed aggregation.
No uncertainty, null comparison, lag analysis, multicollinearity check, or out-of-sample relevance accompanies the near-one relation grades.
The correlation analysis is rhetorically used to promise an enhanced forecast, but its grades never enter a displayed forecasting equation.
The report calls the model enhanced with greenhouse, forest, and population factors, but the displayed GM(1,1) state has only a constant b.
Independent GM(1,1) fits at 225 cells omit spatial dependence and shared ocean dynamics.
One exponential law is extrapolated 50 years without coefficient stability, nonexplosion, or physical temperature bounds.
Directly inverting B^T B receives no rank, conditioning, numerical-stability, or parameter-uncertainty check.
The background-value formula is typographically ambiguous in the rendered source and no numerical example resolves its indices.
No fitted a or b value is reported for even the Table 3 example, so the displayed forecast cannot be reproduced.
The response equation receives no special treatment for a near zero, where b/a is unstable.
The printed response indices and prose alternate x-hat superscripts/subscripts without a consistent one-step horizon convention.
The report does not show how monthly archive values become the annual X0 sequence used in inverse accumulation.
The appendix publishes SST forecasts only through 2048 for a few columns, not the complete 225-cell path through 2070.
No prediction interval, parameter uncertainty, residual model, or spatial covariance accompanies the 2045 and 2070 surfaces.
The paper says 20 locations are used as validation but does not identify them or explain whether validation is spatial, temporal, or both.
Table 3 contains 15 years from 2005 through 2019, not a transparent 20-location acceptance calculation.
Only one cell's residual series is shown, so C=0.55 cannot validate all 225 locations.
The paper gives no acceptance threshold or grey accuracy grade, so C=0.55 is not self-evidently a 'small level'.
The 2019 prediction 7.727 C differs from the actual 3.8316 C by 3.8954 C, larger than the actual value itself.
Residuals become persistently negative and grow after 2010, indicating systematic upward forecast bias rather than random error.
The strength claim of higher accuracy contradicts the acknowledged large final-year deviation and lacks a baseline forecast.
The posterior ratio does not test the decision-relevant 2020-2070 extrapolation horizon.
SST, salinity, and bathymetry have different units and are added without normalization, so E has no coherent physical scale.
The equation uses BM while the notation and prose use SD or bathymetry; BM is never defined.
Expert weights are reported without experts, elicitation method, data fit, uncertainty, or external habitat validation.
Although each weight row sums to one, this does not make unscaled inputs comparable.
The 1980-2018 mean salinity and depth fields are frozen for 50 years while only SST changes, making temperature dominate future score changes by construction.
The SST source is described here as ICES data despite the earlier Hadley archive statement, and the interface between sources is not explained.
Five-year catch maps are treated as habitat observations without correcting for fishing effort, fleet access, quota, or market targeting.
Table 5 comfort intervals are said to come from the longest living environment and previous studies, but no derivation or species data are shown.
The prose says the example fish prefers index 6.75, the Figure 4 center is 6.2, and both exceed or conflict with the displayed species comfort limits.
The broad Table 5 interval and separate absolute tolerance 0.1 define two incompatible stay rules without precedence.
The single optimum E_opt required by the 0.1 rule is never reported for either species.
The assumptions allow movement within two grids per year, but the described 3x3 neighborhood permits only one cell from the center.
No rule handles ties, coast/land candidates, domain edges, diagonals, or a local optimum that traps the greedy path.
A one-cell move has different kilometers in latitude, longitude, and diagonal directions, but all choices are treated equally.
The model moves only one center per species and has no population mass, spread dynamics, births, deaths, or multiple subpopulations.
Initializing at the most-fished cell confounds biological abundance with historical effort and ignores uncertainty in the five-year map.
The claimed onset around 2040 is read from the generated path but receives no threshold, changepoint calculation, or observed migration validation.
Mackerel is variously described as moving toward Canada, Iceland, and through the Faroe Islands without one coordinate endpoint ledger.
Herring is routed toward Norway/Arctic waters but later repeatedly placed at 'South Shetland Islands,' a different hemisphere.
Migration omits currents, prey, spawning, fishing mortality, salinity change, depth accessibility, density feedback, and species interaction.
The upper and lower SST paths used as best and worst cases have no confidence level, residual construction, or probability.
Calling the central path 'most likely' is unsupported because the grey model supplies no forecast distribution.
A circular Gaussian in latitude-longitude degrees is not a physical circle because degree width varies with latitude.
The three-grid radius is uncalibrated and corresponds to hundreds of kilometers, materially controlling catch persistence.
The text alternates between the center as maximum catch and total fish as the Gaussian scale, so density normalization is ambiguous.
No standard deviation, truncation normalization, population conservation, growth, fishing depletion, or catchability is defined.
The cited 90/120-km fishing observation is converted into a hard universal technical limit without vessel, port, route, or preservation heterogeneity.
Distance is measured from the mainland rather than actual ports and navigable sea routes.
The statement that any shoal overlap makes the total fish catchable ignores partial overlap, effort, capacity, and travel cost.
First exact zero catch is an unstable threshold and is not the official economic-impracticality criterion.
Question marks in Table 7 are right-censored beyond 2070 but receive no survival-analysis or uncertainty treatment.
The 2044, 2063, and 2068 dates inherit undocumented SST bounds, score weights, local path ties, shoal radius, and fishing-mask assumptions.
The public article repeatedly calls loss from the modeled Scottish fishing area 'extinction,' a much stronger biological claim.
TFC is a fleet-level cost based on 2.5 percent of all EU vessels, not a small-company cost.
The 2.5-percent Scottish share is held fixed while the appendix forecasts a large decline in EU vessel count through 2069.
TFP is defined in the notation as average income per boat but Q_i P_i appears to use total accessible species catch.
Prices are written as GBP 1,070 and GBP 337 per thousand tons, an implausible and ambiguous unit not reconciled to Q_i.
Costs are in euros and revenue in pounds, but no exchange rate or common currency is applied before subtraction.
The species-specific equation subtracts the full fleet cost from each species separately and does not define combined company profit.
The prose says fleet cost is weighted by species value but publishes no weighting equation or values.
CoS is frozen at the 2010-2015 average through 2070 with no inflation, fuel price, wage, maintenance, or technology path.
No trip count, effort, quota, capacity, spoilage, demand, tax, debt, asset, cash, or company heterogeneity enters net profit.
The CFR forecast from 2020 to 2069 has no disclosed method, fit, equation, validation, or uncertainty.
A declining CFR mechanically lowers total modeled cost and can create the pre-2040 profit increase without any technology mechanism.
The conclusion attributes early profit growth to technology development, but technology is absent from all profit equations.
The report says costs remain stable while simultaneously recommending higher-cost long-endurance technology, without a scenario cost update.
The claimed worst zero-profit year around 2054 is not reconciled with the species-specific 2044 and 2068 zero-catch dates.
The mackerel domestic plot starts near 0.8 billion GBP while the prose calls it about 80 million, a roughly tenfold mismatch.
Market saturation and competition are invoked to explain a domestic decline but neither mechanism appears in the profit equation.
Immediate relocation of all west-coast assets has no port, property, permit, labor, financing, downtime, or market-delivery cost.
The 20-percent-every-five-years schedule is asserted without optimization, cash-flow simulation, or asset inventory.
The 50-percent long-endurance fleet share is asserted without capacity, purchase price, operating cost, or alternative-share comparison.
The paired catch-and-refrigeration vessel logistics omit rendezvous, transfer capacity, fuel, crew, safety, weather, and spoilage constraints.
The claim that doubling preservation time doubles range and increases catch exponentially has no equation, data, or capacity boundary.
The balance-sheet policy has no balance-sheet variables, solvency threshold, capital budget, or decision rule.
The recommended countries depend on species routes but legal access and the requested fishery proportion are not modeled.
The text alternates between Shetland Islands near Scotland and South Shetland Islands near Antarctica, making the domestic destination geographically incoherent.
The public article repeats South Shetland as a domestic Scottish destination, confirming the geographic error rather than a single typo.
One coefficient multiplies cost to represent tariffs, bilateral rules, currents, winds, navigation risk, and unexpected losses with incompatible units and mechanisms.
Norway 1.2 and Iceland 1.5 are designated without source rows, estimation, currency basis, uncertainty, or time dependence.
The existence or absence of Scottish fishing cooperation is asserted without treaty, quota, or licensing evidence.
The official requirement varies the proportion of fishery entering foreign territorial water; the model instead selects whole country destinations and has no proportion variable.
Foreign catch fields near Norway, Iceland, or the claimed South Shetland location are not published or derived from a territorial mask.
Only cost is multiplied; quotas, access limits, tariffs on revenue, port distance, foreign landing price, and legal exclusion do not change.
Figures 9 and 10 cannot be reproduced from the disclosed equations, partial appendix tables, or any code.
The prose says foreign mackerel profit begins lower at 0.5 billion than domestic profit stated as 80 million, which is arithmetically false unless the domestic text is wrong.
The foreign profit slope is described as a consequence of resistance, but a constant cost multiplier alone does not establish the claimed dynamic slope mechanism.
The conclusion that only going abroad is inevitable omits domestic technology costs, switching costs, policy uncertainty, quotas, and alternative fisheries.
Perturbing expert weights independently by 0.1 percent does not state whether the rows are renormalized to sum to one.
Endpoint displacement is measured in Euclidean degrees rather than kilometers and ignores longitude convergence.
A plus or minus 0.1-percent local perturbation is too narrow to represent uncertainty in expert weights or comfort bounds.
A 0.1-percent fishing-radius change is only 0.12 km, so the reported small catch response is not a demanding robustness test.
Country resistance coefficients are likewise moved only 0.1 percent despite being arbitrary scenario assumptions.
Average annual profit response can hide a change in crossover year or strategy ranking.
No joint parameter uncertainty, structural alternative, stochastic replication, or decision-reversal frequency is tested.
The resistance sensitivity table duplicates the Table 9 number already used for coefficient values.
The Hook Line and Sinker article spans roughly two and a half physical pages, exceeding the official one-page requirement.
The article says countless currents, winds, predators, and prey were comprehensively considered, although the migration update changes only SST.
The article claims at least a 2 C rise by 2050 even in the best case without a displayed location, aggregation, or uncertainty calculation supporting that number.
The article gives a 2056 fail-to-make-ends-meet date that is not explicitly derived or tabulated in the body.
The article presents uncosted asset percentages and vessel collaboration as a recipe for earnings rather than as unvalidated proposals.
Appendix maps and the foreign-landings graphic have no adjacent source attribution or license statement.
The appendix provides no executable code for SST forecasting, migration, catch, profit, assets, resistance, or sensitivity.
The partial CFR table stops at 2069 while the modeled horizon and conclusions extend through 2070.
